notes: All seven web searches ran (six required plus one extra). Searches with his name and AI risk terms returned only results about other people, mostly the researcher Stuart Russell; none mentioned Rep. Russell Fry of South Carolina. The fry.house.gov search found no AI statement; it showed only that his vote record lists a Yea vote on H.R. 7757, the AI Warnings And Resources for Education Act (a vote, not a statement; contents not checked). From the earlier attempt (still valid): pages on fry.house.gov were opened directly, namely the home page, the issues page and press release listing pages 1 to 3 (https://fry.house.gov/news/documentquery.aspx?DocumentTypeID=27, then &Page=2 and &Page=3), covering releases from 14 May 2025 to 1 October 2026; no release title or excerpt mentions AI. The 5 December 2025 release on the Kids Internet Safety Partnership Act (https://fry.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=1015) mentions chatbots only in a bullet list of the bill's areas, not in his own words, and is about children's online safety (a D topic at most). He sits on the Energy and Commerce Communications and Technology subcommittee, but no hearing remarks on AI risk were found. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act: the Congress.gov cosponsor page (assumed to be H.R. 10538, per another record in this project) returned 403 again, so co-sponsorship could not be checked directly; no source found shows that he sponsored or co-sponsored it. No House letter about AI risk signed or led by him was found (the many-signer August and September 2026 letters were not searched, per instructions).
